headline: What to Do When Your Bathroom Sink Plumbing Doesn't Line Up
articleBody: It's a common scenario: you've picked out a beautiful new sink or vanity, but when you go to install it, the plumbing just doesn't line up with the existing rough-ins. Don't panic! This is a pretty frequent issue, especially in older homes or when upgrading to a different style of fixture. The first thing to consider is whether you're dealing with a simple misalignment that can be fixed with flexible supply lines or drain extensions, or if you need to actually reposition the supply or drain lines themselves. If it's the latter, that's where things get a bit more complex. You'll need to carefully assess if the old drain/supply layout can stay, or if you're looking at a project that requires moving pipes, which often means opening up walls. While some minor adjustments can be DIY-friendly, moving existing lines or creating new rough-ins definitely warrants bringing in a qualified plumber. They've got the expertise to ensure everything is up to code, leak-free, and properly coordinated with any other work happening in your bathroom. It's all about making sure your new setup works as beautifully as it looks.
